newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - July 7.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy. FRATERNITE MATIN - Ivory Coast's small and medium-sized business sector highlights problems obtaining credit from banks; government plans a guarantee fund in a year and is studying idea of creating a dedicated investment bank for the sector _ European Union and Ivory Coast sign new three-year fishing deal; deal raises number of EU ships fishing in Ivorian waters to 63 from 55 and the quota of tuna they can catch from 7,500 tonnes to 8,500 tonnes - West African CFA franc zone Central Bank governor Charles Konan Banny says conditions ripe for the cost of credit in the eight-nation West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA) to fall; expresses regret that excess liquidity in banks does not find its way into private investment; says Gambia and Guinea should join UEMOA which went from seven to eight members in May when Guinea-Bissau joined - Ivorian transit company SIS-TRANSMIT publishes full-page "information letter" saying needlessly heavy-handed customs checks make it difficult for it, as a small or medium sized national operator, to function; says it has nothing to hide and that it is paying price for dishonest operators in the sector; denounces unfair competition from international operators. LA VOIE - Former head of the Caisse Autonome d'Amortissement, which manages Ivory Coast's national debt, Coulibaly N'Golo, tells seminar that debt forgiveness has to be part of any plans to ease developing countries' debt burdens. LE JOUR - Leader of Renaissance wing of opposition Ivorian Popular Front (FPI) Ahoua Don Mello discussed broad-based government with President Henri Konan Bedie's cabinet director but restated the opposition's party's electoral reform conditions and called for an immediate halt to privatisations. (1$=590 CFA) -- Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90
